    FAPD-AI: Six nonbinary individuals from Puerto Rico challenged the commonwealth's birth certificate gender change application, which restricted options to "Female" or "Male," alleging violations of their Fourteenth Amendment equal protection and due process rights and First Amendment rights. The district court granted summary judgment for the plaintiffs, finding the policy violated the Equal Protection Clause, but the First Circuit Court of Appeals vacated the judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-01245 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-01245-0

    FAPD-AI: A Tenth Circuit court reversed a district court's suppression of evidence, holding that a Colorado trooper had probable cause to arrest a driver for failing to present proof of insurance during a traffic stop. The court ruled that when a driver and vehicle owner did not present required insurance documentation within a reasonable time, the officer's warrantless search incident to the arrest was lawful. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-06137 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-06137-0

    FAPD-AI: A Tenth Circuit court affirmed a 180-month prison sentence imposed on a gang member convicted of maiming another person in aid of racketeering.     Satnam v. Blanche (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-09573 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-09573-0

    FAPD-AI: A Tenth Circuit court dismissed a petition for appellate review of an immigration custody determination for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.     FAPD-AI: A Third Circuit court affirmed the denial of a motion to suppress evidence from a search of a duplex property conducted under a warrant that did not specify which apartment to search.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03012 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03012-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the conviction of Diego Aleman-Lozano, a nonimmigrant visa holder, under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(5)(B), which prohibits nonimmigrant visa holders from possessing firearms. Aleman-Lozano challenged the statute as facially unconstitutional under the Second Amendment, but the court upheld it, applying the framework established in New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass'n v. Bruen to determine whether the statute is consistent with the nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of a civil rights action filed by Bruce Norton, proceeding pro se, seeking relief after state foreclosure proceedings resulted in a sheriff's sale of his property.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02118 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02118-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a district court's denial of a motion to suppress evidence in a drug possession case. A state trooper entered an apartment without a warrant to secure drugs, though his search warrant and tracker order authorized entry only to a different apartment. The court held that the trooper's conduct violated the Fourth Amendment but that suppression was not warranted because the violation constituted isolated negligence rather than deliberate or grossly negligent misconduct. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal of claims brought by the daughter and grandson of Arnie Bell Jennings against relatives alleged to have exploited her cognitive decline to drain her assets after convincing her to move to Oklahoma.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-24-02125 / USCOURTS-ca3-24-02125-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit affirmed Joseph Berger's convictions for possessing thirteen unregistered automatic weapons and a dozen unregistered silencers discovered during a search of his Pennsylvania home. The court held that the Second Amendment does not protect machine gun possession because such weapons are not in common use for lawful purposes, are unsuited to self-defense due to controllability issues, and are principally used for criminal purposes rather than self-defense. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit reversed a summary judgment dismissal of Title IX claims brought by three female basketball players against Eastern New Mexico University for their exposure to sexual harassment by Glen de los Reyes, an individual providing biomechanics treatments to student athletes.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-02118 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-02118-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of a default judgment motion filed by pro se plaintiff John Crowe against three federal probation officers. The response deadline for the defendants began when the United States Attorney was served on November 4, 2024, not when the defendants were initially served on September 18, 2024. The defendants timely filed a responsive motion to dismiss within the court-granted extension and were not subject to default. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Spiehs v. Larsen, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-03061 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-03061-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed dismissal of a First Amendment lawsuit challenging Justin Spiehs's removal from two Lawrence, Kansas City Commission meetings. Spiehs was evicted for allegedly violating the city's requirement that public comments be germane to the commission's business and comply with decorum standards. Because Spiehs failed to adequately preserve his challenge to the decorum standard and failed to adequately challenge the germane standard, he could not demonstrate his evictions were unconstitutional. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    United States v. Bayne (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-04132 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-04132-0

    FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit dismissed Mark Bayne's interlocutory appeal challenging a psychiatric evaluation order for lack of jurisdiction. Bayne was charged with making threats in interstate commerce via a Department of Veterans Affairs communication system. The court held that an order for psychiatric evaluation of an already-detained defendant does not meet the requirements of the collateral-order doctrine for immediate appeal because the individual's interest in avoiding the intrusion does not outweigh the public interest in prompt trials. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Robert Bergdahl v. USA (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-caDC-24-05154 / USCOURTS-caDC-24-05154-0

    FAPD-AI: The United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit held that Article III district courts lack jurisdiction to collaterally review and vacate court-martial judgments. The court remanded Bergdahl's case for dismissal for lack of jurisdiction, finding that while narrow avenues of collateral review exist for military prisoners—such as habeas corpus petitions and Tucker Act claims—none confer authority to vacate the military judgment itself. Bergdahl had challenged his court-martial conviction for desertion and misbehavior before the enemy based on alleged unlawful command influence from statements made by Senator John McCain and then-candidate Donald Trump. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Medical Imaging & Technology Alliance, et al v. Library of Congress, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-caDC-25-05328 / USCOURTS-caDC-25-05328-0

    FAPD-AI: The United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit affirmed the lawfulness of a medical device repair exemption to the Digital Millennium Copyright Act's anticircumvention provision. The Librarian of Congress, through triennial rulemaking, authorized circumvention of technological protection measures on medical devices for diagnosis, maintenance, and repair purposes. The court found that the Librarian properly concluded that persons using medical device software would likely be adversely affected by the anticircumvention prohibition in their ability to make non-infringing repairs. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    119 HR 9330 RH: Earned Wage Access Consumer Protection Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9330rh

    FAPD-AI: This bill regulates earned wage access services, requiring providers to offer no-cost access to earned wages within one business day, provide extensive pre-transaction and ongoing disclosures about fees and tips, maintain consumer dispute procedures, and prohibit certain practices including aggressive debt collection, sharing fees with employers, late fees on unpaid advances, and reporting to credit agencies. The bill also requires providers to verify that disbursements do not exceed available earned wages and prohibits discrimination. BILLS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 02:36:37 Eastern time ET
    119 HR 9331 RH: Strengthening Transaction Oversight and Preventing Payments Fraud Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9331rh

    FAPD-AI: This bill amends the Expedited Funds Availability Act to allow depository institutions to delay funds availability for checks or wire transfers when there is reasonable suspicion of fraud, with initial holds up to ten days and extended holds up to forty-five days, and permits the application of availability exceptions for accounts identified as having greater fraud risk for up to sixty days per occurrence. The bill also requires a study of state laws addressing funds availability and fraud safeguards, prohibits overdraft fees for delayed wire transfers when notice was not provided, and creates a right to know when funds are delayed due to fraud holds. BILLS-SEL-01

    Heightened Import Disclosures for Supply Chain Visibility (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY · FR-2026-09-02 / 2026-17926

    official summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is considering amending its regulations to give CBP greater visibility into the supply chains of goods imported into the United States. CBP is seeking comments on new requirements enhancing visibility into the parties involved in the importation of goods; integrating innovative technical solutions for the tracing of supply chains of those goods; and collecting foreign export documentation that foreign exporters are required to submit to the foreign customs authority prior to the exportation of those goods to the United States. With these proposals, CBP seeks to more effectively detect and interdict illicit importations, especially those that are illegally transshipped to evade compliance with U.S. customs and trade laws. FR-SEL-02

    Exemption of Debt Obligations Issued by the European Union Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for Purposes of Tr… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-02 / 2026-17939

    official summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission” or the “SEC”) is proposing an amendment to designate debt obligations issued by the European Union as “exempted securities” for the purposes of marketing and trading futures contracts on those securities in the United States or to U.S. persons. The amendment is designed to permit futures trading on debt obligations issued by the European Union to be regulated as futures on “exempted securities,” subject to the Commodity Exchange Act. The proposal is intended to increase U.S. persons' access to the market for these products, which may improve opportunities for hedging; lower transaction costs; contribute to greater market depth; reduce operational friction; and increase competition. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-17-07, which applies to certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. AD 2021-17-07 requires inspecting for damage of the left and right motive flow (MF) flexible fuel line assemblies (including the flexible hose and shroud assemblies), and replacing damaged parts. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-17-07, the FAA has determined that four additional airplanes may be subject to the unsafe condition. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2021-17-07 and expand the applicability. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02
